key_insight: The paper introduces a spatio-temporal conditional denoising transformer that makes RGBT tracking more robust when one modality is missing. Instead of relying only on imperfect modality reconstruction, it learns to handle both complete and incomplete inputs flexibly.
problem_solved: It addresses the instability and performance drop in RGBT tracking caused by missing modalities, where RGB or thermal features may be absent or unreliable and existing recovery-based methods produce poor-quality representations.
method: Uses a conditional denoising transformer to refine multimodal features under missing-modality conditions.
Models both spatial and temporal cues to preserve tracking consistency across frames.
Supports flexible processing of complete and modality-missing data without depending solely on explicit modality reconstruction.
impact: This improves the robustness of multimodal tracking systems in real-world settings where sensor failures, occlusions, or degraded inputs are common. For practitioners, it offers a more reliable design pattern for building multimodal models that do not break when one input stream is absent.

paper_title: Spatio-Temporal Conditional Denoising Transformer for Modality-Missing RGBT Tracking
paper_authors: Andong Lu, Ziyi Zha, Jiandong Jin, Shihao Li, Chenglong Li
